II. Testing Documentation
1. Scope of Testing

Testing covers authentication and role scope, user media, mission planning and review, waypoint and segment validation, telemetry ingestion and monitoring, incident handling, post-flight reports and advisory AI. Low-level flight-control algorithms and aviation certification are outside the software test scope.

Unit tests exercise business rules and processing functions with deterministic inputs. Integration tests cover API, persistence, scope and provider boundaries. System tests cover the two-role mainflows and recovery scenarios. Flow owners prepare tests; another team member reviews the cases and evidence.

Tests use a disposable database, scoped test accounts, configured route and restriction fixtures, timestamped telemetry replay, and provider/email stubs. Live MAVLink, provider and email behavior require separate integration evidence. The case designs are prepared; no execution results are recorded in this document.
2. Test Strategy

The strategy combines functional and boundary tests, authorization checks, transaction and recovery tests, realtime measurements and usability checks. Each test is linked to its function, controlled inputs, expected result and execution evidence.
2.1 Testing Types

Functional tests use normal, invalid and boundary inputs to verify required outcomes. Authorization tests use distinct Operators and a Manager to verify role and record scope. Reliability tests use duplicate/out-of-order samples, database failure, missing packets and provider errors. Performance tests record latency, loss and workload conditions. Usability tests cover visible feedback, keyboard navigation and desktop/narrow-screen layouts. A case passes only when its expected outcome and evidence agree.
2.2 Test Levels

Unit: deterministic rule, transaction, aggregation and response-processing checks owned by the function author and peer reviewer. Integration: disposable-database/API and provider-stub scenarios owned by the flow owner. System: a tagged Web/API build and controlled telemetry source exercised by the team. Acceptance: nominated mainflows reviewed against agreed requirements with supervisors. The matrix below shows the applicable testing levels.

Automatic flight preparation and workflow ownership

Current ownership: MF1 / WF-01 — NghiaHQ (Ha Quang Nghia), planning and preflight; MF2 / WF-02 — ThongLQ (Le Quoc Thong), realtime monitoring, incidents and flight preparation; MF3 / WF-03 — DucDDA (Dang Dao Anh Duc), post-flight; MF4 / WF-04 — KhanhGNG (Giang Nguyen Gia Khanh), AI assessment. ThongLQ remains team leader and dossier coordinator.
Implemented scope

AutomaticFlightRequested is optional and defaults to false. Changes follow the mission proposal and approval workflow. This release prepares readiness; dispatchEnabled is false. Neither confirmation nor gateway enrollment uploads a mission, arms motors, sends TAKEOFF/AUTO/MISSION_START, or changes the mission to InProgress.
Confirmation conditions

For an approved, opted-in mission with a schedule, the backend opens confirmation at T minus 5 minutes and closes it at the scheduled start. The authenticated operator must keep a visible browser tab online. Presence is sent every 10 seconds and expires after 30 seconds. The selected, unrevoked mission connection must match the active UAV and flight-controller UID, with gateway heartbeat within 30 seconds and telemetry within 15 seconds.
Readiness evidence

Confirmation reruns preflight and binds readiness to the exact plan hash and connection ID. Readiness requires a passing preflight for that hash from the last minute. Changed plan/connection, stale presence or missing telemetry invalidates the conditions; the operator must review and confirm again. Dismissal, a hidden/offline tab or a missed window is not flight consent.
Future execution scope

Autopilot execution remains a separate development phase: firmware/airframe capability detection, mission compilation and upload/read-back, command IDs/deadlines and replay protection, scheduled condition rechecks, local pre-arm/failsafe enforcement, and ACK plus observed flight-state verification. Validate ArduPilot/PX4 SITL, propeller-free bench operation and supervised flight before enabling dispatch. AI advice cannot authorize launch.
Test execution status

The following flight-preparation cases are planned acceptance/regression targets. No execution date, pass result or physical-aircraft evidence is claimed by this document update. MF2 owner ThongLQ coordinates execution; NghiaHQ reviews preflight fixtures; KhanhGNG verifies that AI advice cannot bypass readiness.
AF-01 Opt-in review
Create a mission without the option, then propose an option change. Expect false by default and the approved plan unchanged until review.
AF-02 Window boundaries
Check immediately before T-5, at T-5, immediately before start, and at start using backend time. Expect confirmation only within [T-5, start).
AF-03 Identity and scope
Try another owner, wrong UAV/UID, revoked/expired connection and inactive UAV. Expect denial or blocked readiness; no aircraft command.
AF-04 Freshness

Exercise stale operator presence (>30 s), gateway heartbeat (>30 s) and telemetry (>15 s), and restore them independently. Missing prerequisites must remain visible; restoring one must not bypass the others.
AF-05 Evidence changes
Confirm, then change plan hash or connection, or expire the passing preflight (>1 minute). Expect earlier evidence not to authorize readiness for changed/stale inputs.
AF-06 Dismiss and disconnect
Dismiss/cancel; hide the tab; lose Internet/session; reconnect after the window. Expect no implied consent or late launch, and cancel clears saved confirmation/presence.
AF-07 Plan contract
Export as owner and non-owner; verify units, waypoint order, altitude reference, E7 conversion and dispatchEnabled=false. Reject unauthorized export; do not interpret a missing altitude as zero.
AF-08 No dispatch
Confirm with all prerequisites and inspect gateway traffic and mission state. Expect no mission upload, ARM, TAKEOFF, mode/start command or readiness-driven InProgress transition.
